q: Which is NO'T a component of a suspended ceiling system?
n: Suspended ceiling systems use wall angles, hangers and runners. Sheathing belongs to wall and roof framing. Source: ASTM C635/C636 (suspended ceiling grid).

q: A resort project in a coastal area of Palawan requires suspended ceiling fasteners that can withstand continuous exposure to salt-laden air, high humidity, and accelerated corrosion during the summer months. The specification emphasizes long-term durability, resistance to pitting, and suitability for environments with chloride contamination. Which fastener material is most appropriate for this application?
n: Type 316 stainless steel, which contains molybdenum, resists chloride pitting in coastal salt air better than 304. Source: ASTM A240; Nickel Institute (stainless steel in marine environments).

q: An office fit-out requires a ceiling system that allows rapid access to mechanical and electrical services for routine maintenance. The architect specifies a system that must permit selective removal of individual panels without damaging adjacent components, ensuring minimal deconstruction during troubleshooting of HVAC, IT cabling, and fire-protection lines. Which ceiling support system best satisfies these requirements?
n: A T-runner suspended grid with lay-in panels lets individual panels be lifted out for service access. Source: ASTM C635; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: Gypsum Board is also known as
n: Gypsum board (plasterboard, wallboard) is also called drywall because it is installed dry, unlike wet plaster. It has a gypsum core faced with paper. Source: ASTM C1396; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: What is the recommended gypsum board thickness for high-rise commercial buildings, particularly for fire-rated partitions walls requiring enhanced durability and safety?
n: Fire-rated partitions commonly use 16 mm (5/8 in.) Type X gypsum board. Source: ASTM C1396 (Type X); GA-600 Fire Resistance Design Manual.

q: Lightweight material used to support gypsum boards.
n: Metal furring (light-gauge steel channels) is the lightweight framing that gypsum boards are fastened to. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 10 (Gypsum Board – Metal Furring).

q: Which material is now popularly used as cladding at building facades?
n: Aluminum composite (cladding) panels are two thin aluminum skins bonded to a core. They are now widely used on building facades. Source: Allen & Iano, Fundamentals of Building Construction, Ch. 21 (Metal Panel Cladding).

q: Which board is now commonly used for ceilings?
n: Gypsum board, a gypsum core faced with paper and fixed to furring, is the common ceiling and partition board. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 10 (Gypsum Board).

q: Which material is specifically designed to reduce sound transmission, absorb sound and improve the acoustics of a room, and is now commonly used in music studios, theaters, conference rooms, home theaters and office spaces?
n: Acoustic boards are porous or perforated panels made to absorb sound and reduce its transmission. They improve room acoustics in studios, theaters, conference rooms and offices. Source: Egan, Architectural Acoustics; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 10 (Acoustical Ceilings).

q: Also known as edge beams, these beams are located at the outer edges of a building. The space between them allow for architectural flexibility. as it allows various materials to be installed to form the building exterior facade such as masonry, concrete, glass, cladding and other architectural elements and finishes.
n: Spandrel (edge) beams run along the outer edges of each floor. The facade materials and finishes fill the space between them. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: Which of the following does not transfer vertical loads nor carry weight and is simply used to enclose building envelopes
n: A precast concrete curtain wall only encloses the building. It carries no floor loads, unlike bearing CMU or shear walls. Source: PCI Architectural Precast Concrete Manual; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: What surveying work is done when determining the property Lines of a site
n: A boundary survey establishes a site's property lines. Source: DENR Manual for Land Surveys in the Philippines (DAO 2007-29).

q: During site layout, the survey team needs to measure both horizontal and vertical angles to establish precise control points for the building footprint. Which instrument is used for this purpose?
n: A transit or theodolite measures horizontal and vertical angles to set control points. Source: Ghilani & Wolf, Elementary Surveying, Ch. 8.

q: A carpenter is installing door jambs and must ensure that the frame is perfectly level and plumb before fastening. Which tool is used to check alignment?
n: A spirit level checks that a frame is level and plumb. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (construction tools).

q: A mason needs to transfer a vertical reference line from the beam down to the floor to align a column formwork. Which tool is used to establish a true vertical line?
n: A plumb bob hangs on a string to transfer a true vertical line from above to the floor. Source: Ghilani & Wolf, Elementary Surveying.

q: During the early stages of construction, the survey team needs to transfer the building's footprint from the plans to the actual ground. They must establish permanent reference points above the excavation level so that the building lines, corners, and elevations can be rechecked even after digging begins. A setup is used to hold string lines that define the exact layout of the structure. What is this layout system called?
n: Batter boards are set outside the excavation and hold the string lines that mark building lines, corners and levels. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (site layout).

q: The contractor must excavate deep trenches for drainage and utility lines. The machine has a fully rotating upper structure, a boom-stick-bucket assembly, and is typically mounted on tracks for stability during heavy digging operations. Which piece of equipment is this?
n: An excavator has a fully rotating upper structure, a boom-stick-bucket arm and usually tracks, for heavy trench digging. Source: Peurifoy, Construction Planning, Equipment, and Methods, Ch. 8.

q: In site works, accurate column placement is essential to maintain structural alignment and prevent foundation errors. Various methods are used to establish precise reference points before excavation begins. Among the following options, which is the primary reference system used to determine the centerline of columns in construction layouts?
n: Column centerlines are set out from the grid lines on the structural layout. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (layout); Ghilani & Wolf, Elementary Surveying (construction surveying).

q: In a typical building construction sequence, which activity should be completed immediately before excavation begins?
o: Conducting a geotechnical investigation to determine soil bearing capacity and water table level
Mobilizing excavation equipment and verifying access routes for hauling and spoil disposal
Clearing vegetation and debris from the site to expose the natural ground
Establishing offset stakes and batter boards to define excavation boundaries and depth
n: Offset stakes and batter boards marking the excavation limits and depth are set just before digging starts. Clearing and soil investigation come earlier. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (site preparation sequence).

q: The following CHB sizes are commercially available except
n: Locally, CHB comes in 4-, 5-, 6- and 8-inch widths. 10-inch blocks are not commonly available. Source: PNS 16 (Concrete Hollow Blocks).

q: What is a masonry wall where CHB and bricks are bonded together for better appearance?
n: A composite masonry wall bonds two kinds of units, such as CHB backup with brick facing, into one wall. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (masonry); NCMA TEK notes; TMS 402 (composite masonry).

q: A decorative, non-load-bearing wall covering installed over a structural wall primarily to enhance appearance while replicating the aesthetic of natural stone is known as
n: Stone veneer is a non-load-bearing facing over a structural wall that copies the look of natural stone. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (masonry); NCMA TEK notes (veneer).

q: A local CHB manufacturing plant is under pressure to double its daily output due to a large government housing contract. The production manager needs a curing method that will allow newly molded blocks to reach safe handling strength within hours, enabling rapid turnover of steel molds and minimizing storage time. The method must accelerate cement hydration without compromising early-age strength, and must be feasible in a controlled factory environment. Which curing method best satisfies these requirements?
n: Steam curing speeds up hydration so CHB reach handling strength within hours, allowing fast mold turnover in the plant. Source: ACI 517.2R (accelerated curing of concrete masonry units).

q: During the inspection of a load-bearing brick wall. the foreman notices that several joints lack sufficient mortar and reminds the crew of its intended function. in masonry construction, what ts the primary purpose of mortar?
o: Increase the thermal mass of the wall
Serve as a decorative joint filler
n: Mortar binds masonry units together and transfers loads between them. Source: ASTM C270; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (masonry); NCMA TEK notes.

q: In masonry construction, block-laying techniques determine both structural integrity and visual appeal. While some methods enhance load distribution, others focus on pattern aesthetics. Which technique uniquely deviates from the standard horizontal positioning, often misinterpreted due to its use in facades and decorative structures?
n: A soldier course sets units upright on end instead of in the usual horizontal position. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (masonry); NCMA TEK notes (brick positions).

q: Different masonry bonding techniques influence the strength, stability and visual continuity of a wall. While some maximize interlocking for durability, others focus on achieving a clean, grid-like appearance with perfectly aligned joints. Which technique aligns blocks in direct vertical columns without staggering. creating a modern aesthetic but requiring additional reinforcement for structural integrity?
n: Stack bond lines units up in vertical columns with continuous head joints. It needs joint reinforcement. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (masonry); NCMA TEK notes; TMS 402 (stack bond reinforcement).

q: Masonry bonding patterns play a crucial role in a wall's structural stability and load distribution. While some techniques prioritize strength through interlocking headers, others rely on efficient staggered joints to prevent vertical weaknesses. Which bonding method achieves superior strength and stress distribution by staggering blocks in a continuous, offset pattern across the entire structure?
n: Running bond offsets each course by half a unit, spreading stress and avoiding continuous vertical joints. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (masonry); NCMA TEK notes.

q: While some techniques emphasize aesthetics or simple alignment, others maximize strength through strategic alternation of rows. Which method utilizes full courses of both headers and stretchers, creating a highly durable structure known for its ability to resist heavy loads and ensure long-term stability?
n: English bond alternates full courses of headers and stretchers, making a very strong wall. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (masonry); NCMA TEK notes.

q: Masonry bonding techniques significantly impact both structural strength and aesthetic complexity. While some methods prioritize sheer load-bearing capacity, others integrate an interlocking system that improves both durability and visual appeal. Which technique alternates between headers and stretchers within each row, creating a pattern that strengthens the entire structure?
n: Flemish bond alternates headers and stretchers within each course, interlocking the wythes. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (masonry); NCMA TEK notes.

q: In masonry construction, certain blocks are designed to soften sharp edges, improving both aesthetics and safety in exposed areas. Which type of block is specifically shaped to provide a rounded finish at corners or edges, commonly used in window sills and decorative applications?
n: Bullnose blocks have rounded edges, for corners, sills and decorative uses. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (masonry); NCMA TEK notes (special units).

q: Masonry blocks serve specific structural roles, allowing for transition between sections of a wall. While some block types prioritize reinforcement or aesthetics, others are designed to ensure proper alignment and connectivity at key junctions. Which block type is specifically shaped to integrate seamlessly at wall intersections, maintaining structural continuity?
n: Corner blocks have a finished end that keeps the wall continuous at corners and intersections. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (masonry); NCMA TEK notes (CMU shapes).

q: Masonry blocks serve specialized functions beyond simple stacking, with some playing a crucial role in reinforcing structural openings. While certain types prioritize aesthetics or vertical strength, others are designed to support horizontal spans, preventing collapse where standard blocks cannot provide direct load transfer. Which type of block is specifically shaped to strengthen openings above doors and windows, efficiently distributing weight?
n: Lintel (U-shaped) blocks are grouted and reinforced to span door and window openings. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (masonry); NCMA TEK notes (CMU shapes).

q: A contractor is selecting a masonry material for interior partition walls in a mid-rise residential project. The material must be lightweight, economical, uniform in size, and easy to cut for electrical and plumbing chases. It should also allow fast laying using semi-skilled labor and provide consistent wall thickness. The architect prefers a manufactured unit made from fired clay with predictable strength and dimensions. Which material best fits these requirements?
n: Fired-clay brick is uniform, predictable in strength and dimension, easy to cut and quick to lay. Source: ASTM C62/C216 (building and facing brick).

q: Horizontal reinforcing bars play a crucial role in CHB wall construction, enhancing structural integrity and resistance to forces. However, one of the following ts NOT a primary purpose of horizontal reinforcement in CHB masonry. Which one is it?
o: Reducing cracks caused by shrinkage and thermal expansion
Resisting lateral forces such as earthquakes and wind loads
Increasing the compressive strength of individual CHB blocks
Distributing loads evenly to prevent localized stress points
n: Horizontal bars resist lateral forces, spread loads and control shrinkage cracks. They do not raise the compressive strength of the individual blocks. Source: TMS 402; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (masonry); NCMA TEK notes.

q: According to DPWH, which class applies to grouted riprap described as "ranging from 15 kg to 25 kg, with at least 50 percent of the stones weighing more than 20 kg"?
n: DPWH Class A grouted riprap uses stones of 15–25 kg, at least half of them over 20 kg. Source: DPWH Standard Specifications, Item 505 (Riprap and Grouted Riprap).

q: A slope stabilization project in a flood-prone area of Manila requires a retaining structure that remains permeable to flowing water while resisting erosion during heavy monsoon runoff. The design calls for a system that can dissipate hydraulic pressure, allow drainage through the structure, and be constructed using steel wire mesh units filled with stones sourced from a nearby quarry. Which type of structure best fits this requirement?
n: Gabions are stone-filled steel wire mesh units. They stay permeable, dissipate water pressure and resist erosion. Source: ASTM A975; DPWH Item 511.

q: What is the most common mortar used in masonry in the Philippines?
n: Cement-sand mortar is the most common masonry mortar in the Philippines. Source: DPWH Item 1046; local masonry practice.

q: What is the most common type of cement in general use?
n: Portland cement is the most common general-use cement. Source: ASTM C150; Neville, Properties of Concrete.

q: Which type of cement contains siliceous or aluminous materials that react with calcium hydroxide to improve long-term durability, reduce permeability, and is commonly used in blended formulations for sustainable construction?
n: Pozzolan cement contains siliceous or aluminous materials that react with calcium hydroxide. This improves durability, lowers permeability and suits sustainable blended mixes. Source: ASTM C595 (blended cements).

q: Which type of cement is primarily composed of calcium silicates and is produced by heating limestone and clay in a kiln, forming the basis for most modern concrete mixes?
n: Portland cement, mainly calcium silicates from kiln-burned limestone and clay, is the basis of most concrete. Source: ASTM C150.

q: Steel reinforcement in non-load bearing masonry walls serves what purpose?
o: To transfer loads from the top structure
n: Reinforcement in non-load-bearing masonry mainly keeps the walls from failing (cracking or toppling) during earthquakes. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 7 (masonry seismic requirements); TMS 402.

q: A CHB wall may function as a load-bearing wall when it is
n: A CHB wall can act as a load-bearing wall when it is reinforced and grouted (reinforced masonry). Source: NSCP 2015, Ch. 7; TMS 402.

q: In a composite floor system, which component is used to transfer shear forces between the concrete slab and the steel beam?
n: Shear connectors (headed studs welded to the beam flange) transfer horizontal shear between the concrete slab and the steel beam so that they act compositely. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 509 (Composite Members); Allen & Iano, Fundamentals of Building Construction, Ch. 11.

q: In a composite floor system, which component enhances adhesion between concrete and steel, increases shear resistance, provides structural strength and acts as formwork?
n: Profiled (composite) steel deck sheeting acts as permanent formwork and tensile reinforcement. Its embossments improve bond with the concrete and add shear resistance. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 509; Allen & Iano, Fundamentals of Building Construction, Ch. 11 (Composite Metal Decking).

q: What is used to connect steel to steel?
n: A gusset plate connects steel members to each other, as at truss joints and bracing. Source: AISC Steel Construction Manual, Part 9 (gusset plates).

q: An elegant and versatile material that combines the aesthetic appeal of wood with the durability of plastic. It is crafted from finely ground wood fibers (such as sawdust) and thermoplastic resins (such as PVC or uPVC). The ingredients are mixed and heated, then extruded or molded into various shapes and sizes. Pigments, binding agents and lubricants are added to enhance strength and properties. It is extremely popular for both indoor and outdoor paneling applications.
n: WPC (wood-plastic composite) is made of fine wood fibers and thermoplastic resins (PVC or uPVC), extruded or molded for indoor and outdoor paneling. Source: ASTM D7032 (wood-plastic composite decking).

q: A resort development along the coast requires a decking material for outdoor terraces, poolside walkways, and viewing decks. The material must replicate the appearance of wood while providing superior resistance to moisture, fading, staining, mold growth, and weathering. Which type of decking is most appropriate for this application?
n: Capped composite decking looks like wood and resists moisture, fading, staining, mold and weathering, which suits coastal resorts. Source: ASTM D7032; manufacturer data.

q: Which hand-held power tool is used for sanding various surfaces, has a round pad that rotates in an elliptical pattern, and leaves a smooth and even finish without circular swirl marks?
n: A random orbital sander has a round pad that spins while moving in an elliptical orbit, so it sands evenly without swirl marks. Source: Fine Woodworking tool references; Spence, Carpentry and Building Construction (Power Tools).

q: Which powerful, aggressive tool is designed for fast wood removal, consists of a pair of rotating drums carrying a continuous loop of sandpaper, and operates in a linear motion?
n: A belt sander runs a continuous loop of abrasive over two drums in a linear motion. It removes wood quickly and aggressively for trimming, leveling and shaping. Source: Spence, Carpentry and Building Construction (Power Tools).

q: Which tool is used for edge profiling or shaping, cutting joints like dadoes, rabbets and mortise-and-tenons, flush trimming, hinge mortising and creating intricate inlays, and is essentially a motor with a sharp spinning bit protruding from the bottom?
n: A router is a motor with a spinning bit that protrudes from its base. It is used for edge profiling, joints (dadoes, rabbets, mortises), flush trimming, hinge mortising and inlays. Source: Spence, Carpentry and Building Construction (Power Tools).
